sentences.text:
MFA No.4712/2018 is filed by the claimant, whereas MFA No.4247/2018 is filed by the Insurance Company under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, (for short, 'the Act') being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 07.02.2018 passed by the Senior Civil Judge & JMFC & XIX MACT,
Chikkanayakanahalli (for short, 'the Tribunal') in MVC No.347/2016.
Since the challenge is to the same judgment, both the appeals are clubbed together, heard and common judgment is being passed.

2. Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeals briefly stated are that on 26.04.2015 at about 10.30 a.m., the claimant, along with his colleagues was proceeding in a bus bearing registration No.KL-58/5500 towards Alase Chowdeshwari temple to attend his friend's sister's marriage.

When they reached near Honnasagadde cross and the bus was in the curve, at that time, one lorry bearing registration No.KA-34/4614 being driven by its driver at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, NC: 2023:KHC:33222 dashed to the backside of the bus in which the claimant was proceeding.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
3. The claimant filed petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses, conveyance, etc.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred purely on account of the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
4. On service of notice, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through counsel and respondent No.2 filed written statement in which the averments made in the petition were denied.
The age, avocation and income of the claimants and the medical expenses are denied.
It was pleaded that the petition itself is false and frivolous in the eye of law.
It was further pleaded that the driver of the lorry was not having a valid and effective driving licence.
It was further pleaded that the liability is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.
It was further NC: 2023:KHC:33222 pleaded that the quantum of compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant.
Hence, he sought for dismissal of the petition.
5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter recorded the evidence.
The claimant examined himself as PW-1 and Dr.Ashwath Acharya was examined as PW-2 and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P175.
On behalf of the respondents, neither any witness was examined nor got exhibited documents.

The Claims Tribunal,
by the impugned judgment, inter alia, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the claimant sustained injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.12,15,565/-
along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, these appeals have been filed.

Sri O.Mahesh, the learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company has raised the following contentions:
Sri Ram General Insurance vs Mohankumar on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34374772/
4

sentences.text: (i) Firstly, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the bus bearing registration No.KL-58/5500.
But the Tribunal has erred in holding that the driver of the lorry is negligent in causing the accident.
(ii) Secondly, even to prove the negligence of the driver of the lorry the claimant has examined himself as PW1.
In his chief-examination, he has categorically stated that the driver of the lorry has come in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the right hind portion of the bus.

(iii) Thirdly, he has taken me through the IMV report and contended that by looking into the IMV report it is very clear that the bus, while negotiating the lorry, dashed to the hind portion of the lorry and it is not the negligence of the driver of the lorry.
Fourthly, as per the IMV report the rear side body of the lorry has been damaged.

In respect of the bus is concerned, the rear right side shape dented and right side window glass broken and it is very clear that the driver of the bus while negotiating the lorry dashed against the lorry.
This aspect of the matter has not been considered by the Tribunal and the Tribunal has erred in holding that the driver of the lorry alone is negligent in causing the accident.
(v) Fifthly, one Harish who is the complainant has not been examined.
Since it is a cross road the driver of the bus came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the lorry.
Without considering this aspect of the matter the Tribunal has erred in holding that the driver of the lorry alone is negligent in causing the accident.

(vi) Sixthly, even though the claimant claims that he was earning Rs.17,322/- per month and produced the salary certificate, he has not examined the employer or the author of the document to prove his income.
Under NC: 2023:KHC:33222 the circumstances, the Tribunal has erred in considering the monthly income of the claimant as Rs.17,322/-.
(vii) Seventhly, the injuries suffered by the claimant are minor in nature.
The doctor has assessed the permanent disability of right upper limb as 69% and the Tribunal rightly assessed the whole body disability at 23% and there is no functional disability.

Even though the claimant has claimed that he was not continued in service, he has not produced any document to show that he has been removed from service or he has resigned and he has not examined the employer to prove that he was not continued in service.
But the Tribunal erred in granting compensation under the head 'loss of future income'.
(viii) Lastly, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the other heads is on the higher side.
Hence, he sought for allowing the appeal filed by the Insurance Company and dismissal of the appeal filed by the claimant.

sentences.text:
Per contra, Sri K.Shantaraj, the learned counsel for the claimant has raised the following contentions:
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:33222
(i) Firstly, the Insurance Company has neither examined any witnesses nor produced any documents to disprove the claim of the claimant.
They have not proved that there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry.
Therefore, the appeal in respect of negligence is concerned, it is not maintainable.

(ii) Secondly, the claimant, who is an eyewitness to the accident, examined himself as PW1 and has clearly stated that the driver of the lorry came from backside and dashed against the bus and due to the impact the claimant has suffered the injuries.
The Tribunal has rightly held that the driver of the lorry was negligent in causing the accident.

(iii) Thirdly, at the time of the accident the deceased was earning Rs.17,322/- per month and he has produced the appointment order, confirmation letter and salary certificate, which have been marked as Exs. P159, P160 and P161.
This amount has been remitted to his bank account.
It clearly shows that he was working in a private - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:33222 company and earning Rs.17,322/- per month.
The Tribunal has rightly assessed the monthly income.

(iv) Fourthly, the claimant has examined the doctor who has deposed that claimant has suffered 69% disability to particular limb and has deposed that due to the disability he was unable to do his day today work.

Even the claimant has deposed that due to disability he is unable to continue his work and he has left the job, therefore, there is 100% disability and the Tribunal has considered the whole body disability at only 23% and has not considered addition of future prospects.

In support of his contentions, he relied on the judgments of the Apex Court in the case of 'PAPPU DEO YADAV vs.
NARESH KUMAR AND OTHERS' 2020 SCC Online SC 752 and 'ERUDHAYA PRIYA vs. STATE EXPRESS TRANSPORT CORPORATION LTD. '2020 SCC Online SC 601'.
(v) Fifthly, the Tribunal has not awarded compensation under the heads 'loss of amenities' and 'loss of income during laid-up period'.

sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award and the original records.

9. The case of the claimant is that on 26.04.2015 at about 10.30 a.m., the claimant, along with his colleagues was proceeding in a bus bearing registration No.KL-58/5500 towards Alase Chowdeshwari temple to attend his friend's sister's marriage.

When they reached near Honnasagadde cross and the bus was in the curve, at that time, one lorry bearing registration No.KA-34/4614 being driven by its driver at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner,
dashed to the backside of the bus in which the claimant was proceeding.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
10. To prove the case, the claimant examined himself as PW1.
In his evidence he has reiterated the averments made in the claim petition.

He has produced FIR,
- 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:33222 complaint, charge sheet, IMV report, wound certificate and other documents.
Even in the course of cross-examination of PW1 nothing has been elicited to disbelieve his evidence.

To disprove the case of the claimant the respondent has neither examined any witnesses nor produced any documents.
11.
Under the Motor Vehicles Act in the claim petition before the Claims Tribunal, the standard of proof is much below than what is required in a criminal case as well as in the civil case.

No doubt,
before the Tribunal, there must be some material on the basis of which the Tribunal can arrive or decide things necessary to decide for awarding compensation, but the Tribunal is not expected to take or to adopt a nicety of a civil or criminal case.
After all it is a summary enquiry and it is the legislation for the welfare of the Society.
The proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are not akin to the proceedings under civil rules.
Hence, strict rules of evidence are not required to be followed in this regard.

In the case of MANGLA RAM -v- ORIENTAL - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:33222 INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED (2018) 5 SCC 656, the Hon'ble Apex Court has held as hereinbelow:
"25.

entities.text: MANGLA RAM -v- ORIENTAL - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:33222 INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED (2018) 5 SCC 656
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Dulcina Fernandes, this Court examined similar situation where the evidence of claimant's eyewitness was discarded by the Tribunal and that the respondent in that case was acquitted in the criminal case concerning the accident.

This Court,
however, opined that it cannot be overlooked that upon investigation of the case registered against the respondent, prima facie, materials showing negligence were found to put him on trial.

The Court restated the settled principle that the evidence of the claimants ought to be examined by the Tribunal on the touchstone of preponderance of probability and certainly the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
Sri Ram General Insurance vs Mohankumar on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/34374772/
7
Therefore, there is no standard of proof required for disproving the case.

In view of the above,
considering the documents produced by the claimant and the evidence, the Tribunal has rightly answered issue No.1 and rightly - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:33222 held that the driver of the lorry was negligent in causing the accident.

Re.quantum:
12. Due to the accident the claimant has suffered dislocation of right elbow and other injuries.
He has examined the doctor as PW2, who in his evidence has deposed that the claimant has suffered 69% disability to particular limb.
Considering the evidence of the doctor and the injuries suffered by the claimant, the Tribunal has rightly assessed the whole body disability at 23%.

In respect of income is concerned, the claimant has produced the appointment order, confirmation letter and the salary certificate which have been marked as Exs. P159, 160 and 161 which clearly shows that he was earning income of Rs.17,322/- per month.
Even in the salary certificate, the name of the Bank along with account number has been shown.
Therefore, the Tribunal has rightly considered the monthly income of the claimant as Rs.17,322/-.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:33222 of PAPPU DEO YADAV (supra) and ERUDHAYA PRIYA (supra), the claimant is entitled for addition of future prospects.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -v- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS [AIR 2017 SC 5157], since the claimant was aged about 31 years, 40% of his income has to be added towards future prospects and the applicable multiplier is '16'.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -v- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS [AIR 2017 SC 5157]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the monthly income of the claimant comes to Rs.24,251/- (Rs.17,322 + 6,929).

Thus, the claimant is entitled to Rs.10,70,924/-
(Rs.24,251x12x16x23%) on account of 'loss of future income due to disability'.
13. Due to the accident, the claimant has suffered grievous injuries.
He was taking treatment from 20.04.2015 to 17.01.2016 as inpatient and outpatient.

Considering the injuries suffered by the claimant, considering the evidence of the doctor and considering the wound certificate, I am of the opinion that the claimant is entitled to 'loss of income during laid-up period' for a period of three months, i.e., 51,966/- (Rs.17,322x3).
The - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:33222 claimant is also entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head 'loss of amenities'.
Considering the nature of injuries, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads is just and reasonable.
14. Thus, the claimant is entitled to the following compensation:

In the result, I pass the following order:
(i) The appeal filed by the claimant, i.e., MFA No.4712/2018 is allowed in part.
(ii) The appeal filed by the Insurance Company, i.e., MFA No.4247/2018 is dismissed.
(iii) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.

(iv) The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of realization, within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
(v) The amount in deposit is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal forthwith.
